backlog.title: Linear Optics And The Push To Scale AI Interconnects
backlog.summary:
Move signal processing back onto the host SerDes to reduce system power, latency, and thermal load. 
The post Linear Optics And The Push To Scale AI Interconnects appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Linear optics are being explored as a method to simplify optical interconnects by moving signal processing back to the host SerDes.
This architectural shift aims to significantly reduce system-level power consumption, latency, and thermal load compared to traditional DSP-based optical modules.
By removing complex signal processing from the optical module, designers can achieve higher port density and better scaling for massive AI clusters.

bullets: The path to widespread deployment of co-packaged optics depends on solving challenges in manufacturing, testing, and operations.
Co-packaged optics (CPO) is at an inflection point.
We see it rapidly transitioning from proof-of-concept prototypes to manufacturable systems.
Today, we’re already starting to see the technology embedded in scale-out switch ASIC packages, where copper can no longer handle the bandwidth-distance requirements.

While the technology shows promise for AI infrastructure by offering multi-generational scaling potential through wavelength multiplication, higher modulation rates, and increased port density, the path to widespread...

backlog.title: Is Pergrammable A Word?
backlog.summary:
SoC architects need AI silicon that is both highly efficient and fully programmable.
The post Is Pergrammable A Word? appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: SoC architects face a 'performance vs. programmability' dilemma, as the state of the art in AI models evolves faster than the two-to-three-year silicon design cycle.
With leading-edge SoC development costs exceeding $200 million, chips must be field-programmable to support future AI models that do not yet exist at the time of tapeout.
The industry is struggling to find IP solutions that provide the high throughput and low power of fixed-function silicon while maintaining the flexibility of software-defined architectures.

backlog.title: Packet-Based NPUs In The LLM Era: From Compute-Bound CNNs To Memory-Bound Edge And Automotive Workloads
backlog.summary:
Vision-only edge processors are giving way to systems where LLMs, VLMs, and generative features sit alongside traditional perception networks. 
The post Packet-Based NPUs In The LLM Era: From Compute-Bound CNNs To Memory-Bound Edge And Automotive Workloads appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Edge and automotive NPU architectures are shifting from compute-bound CNN designs to memory-bound transformer models that require efficient KV cache management.
The transition to LLMs and VLMs in resource-constrained environments renders traditional TOPS-based performance metrics less relevant than memory bandwidth and access patterns.
Packet-based scheduling, originally designed for CNNs, is being adapted to optimize the memory-heavy decode phases of generative AI models.

backlog.title: What Self-Verifying Means In Agentic EDA Workflows And Why It Matters
backlog.summary:
Grounding agent decisions in their output is what transforms orchestration into something engineers can build on with confidence.
The post What Self-Verifying Means In Agentic EDA Workflows And Why It Matters appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: To ensure trust in autonomous EDA workflows, AI agents must be grounded in physics-based, deterministic verification engines at every step of the design process.
Continuous verification allows agents to reason and converge on correct results by interacting directly with EDA tools rather than relying on post-process checks.
This approach is critical for semiconductor design, where tapeout deadlines are rigid and the cost of respins due to unverified agent decisions is prohibitive.

backlog.title: Vertical Integration Becoming Pervasive
backlog.summary:
No system can be optimized without an understanding of both the hardware and software, and making the right architectural choice requires cooperation.  
The post Vertical Integration Becoming Pervasive appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The industry is shifting back toward vertical integration and hardware/software co-design to optimize systems for specific, massive AI workloads.
Modern development cycles are increasingly constrained by software iteration speeds, which currently outpace hardware design, necessitating new virtual twin and prototyping tools.
Custom ASICs are seeing a resurgence as companies move away from generic IP assemblies to achieve the efficiency required for stable, high-performance applications.

backlog.title: What’s behind this summer’s heat, and why 2027 could be worse
backlog.summary: This summer has been a scorcher for much of the Northern Hemisphere. June and July marked the hottest two-month stretch in Europe since record-keeping began. The contiguous US endured its hottest month on record in July. South Korea saw its highest-ever recorded temperature.   The heat isn’t over yet, but some scientists are already looking ahead…
bullets: Record-breaking heat waves across the US, Europe, and South Korea have been exacerbated by climate change, with Europe identified as the world's fastest-warming continent.
Scientists warn that 2027 may see even higher temperatures as the current El Niño event exerts a more significant impact on global climate patterns than it did this year.
The intensity of recent heat waves is historically unprecedented, with US temperatures in July surpassing records set during the 1936 Dust Bowl era.

A researcher was there to unveil the Human Cell Atlas, an ambitious project that aimed to map every cell in the human body. Taylor was floored, and then concerned. As details emerged, she discovered that the…
bullets: The NIH awarded a $38.5 million grant to the Developmental Genotype-Tissue Expression Project (dGTEx) to map healthy pediatric tissue, addressing a critical gap in medical research.
Pediatric researchers emphasize that children are not merely 'small adults,' as distinct gene expression patterns in children can lead to adverse drug reactions that adults do not experience.
The project aims to establish a comprehensive baseline for pediatric development, which is essential for improving drug safety and precision medicine for younger populations.

backlog.title: Defect Prediction in Optical Lithography, EUVL, and NIL (National Taiwan University)
backlog.summary:
National Taiwan University researchers published a technical paper titled “From Lithography to Nanoimprint: Physics-Based, Data-Driven, and Hybrid Frameworks for Defect Prediction in Advanced Patterning Technologies.” Abstract: “Advanced patterning technologies have evolved from direct optical image transfer into predictive manufacturing frameworks in which defects are shaped by imaging physics, material response, process variation, and computational correction.... » read more
The post Defect Prediction in Optical Lithography, EUVL, and NIL (National Taiwan University) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers at National Taiwan University have categorized defect prediction into physics-based, data-driven, and hybrid frameworks to address the complexities of advanced patterning.
The transition from conventional optical lithography to EUVL and Nanoimprint Lithography (NIL) necessitates new modeling approaches due to stochastic resist response and mask 3D effects.
NIL-specific defect challenges, such as template interaction and viscoelastic deformation, require moving beyond traditional geometry-driven correction logic.

Hybrid frameworks combining machine learning with physical constraints are identified as the most promising path for achieving uncertainty-aware, data-efficient defect prediction in next-generation manufacturing.

backlog.title: Scientists just created female clones of male mice
backlog.summary: Scientists have deliberately turned male mouse embryos into females for the first time. A team based in Japan used a CRISPR-based approach to remove the Y chromosome from male cells and create female clones of male mice.  “No one has done this before,” says Monika Ward, a reproductive biologist at the University of Hawaii, who…
bullets: Researchers in Japan have successfully used a CRISPR-based technique to remove the Y chromosome from male mouse embryos, effectively creating female clones of male mice.
The study, currently in preprint, challenges the biological assumption that both male and female gametes are strictly required for mammalian reproduction.
The technology is being positioned as a potential breakthrough for conservation efforts, offering a way to rescue endangered species where only male individuals remain.
While the method shows promise, experts note that cloning remains inefficient and can lead to reduced genetic diversity, which may increase vulnerability to disease in offspring.

backlog.title: How much hydrogen awaits us underground?
backlog.summary: In the 1990s, Barbara Sherwood Lollar descended into the Kidd Creek mine in northern Ontario, which cuts more than three kilometers into the ancient root of North America. There her team of geochemists found water that had been confined underground for more than a billion years. This ancient brine turned out to be a habitat…
bullets: Geologic hydrogen, produced naturally via water-rock reactions or radioactive decay, is being pursued as a zero-carbon fuel source to bypass the high energy costs of traditional hydrogen production.
While the US Geological Survey estimates trillions of tons of hydrogen exist in the Earth's crust, no commercially viable reservoir has been identified to date.
Startups like Koloma and HyTerra are actively exploring the US Midwest, though a lack of public data persists as firms compete for investment and proprietary geological insights.

backlog.title: How kids feel about AI, in their own words
backlog.summary: When we set out to talk to kids about artificial intelligence, we thought we knew what we’d hear. We expected some to tell us they were using it to cheat a little, the way Millennials and Gen Xers opened up CliffsNotes or programmed formulas into their TI-82s, and others to share inspiring ways they were…
bullets: Pew Research data from early 2026 indicates that while 57% of US teens use AI chatbots for information, only 12% utilize them for emotional support or advice.
Many youths express skepticism or indifference toward AI, citing concerns over the erosion of critical thinking, creativity, and the environmental impact of large-scale models.
Unlike consumer hardware or social media, AI is often encountered by younger users passively through existing apps and school-mandated tools rather than through active adoption.

backlog.title: What happens when a kid’s robot best friend dies?
backlog.summary: When Xander first met Moxie, she taught him that when he was anxious, he could calm down by exhaling through his lips so that he buzzed like a bee. They practiced breathing like dragons to manage feeling mad and sniffing like bunnies to boost his energy. But in the six years they’ve known each other,…
bullets: The market for AI-powered companion toys for children is expanding rapidly, with major players like Mattel developing OpenAI-enabled products and significant growth reported in China.
These devices are increasingly marketed to neurodivergent children for social skill development, yet they face long-term viability challenges when manufacturers go out of business.

The reliance on cloud-based AI infrastructure creates a 'dead robot' phenomenon, where devices lose their core functionality and therapeutic utility once the supporting corporate servers are deactivated.

backlog.title: We still don’t know how people are really using AI
backlog.summary: AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI regularly publish reports on how people are using products like Claude and ChatGPT, but they only release the data they want us to see, AI researchers say.  “There is no independent source to corroborate it,” says Anka Reuel, a computer science PhD candidate at the Stanford Trustworthy AI Research…
bullets: The AI Observatory study reveals that nearly 48% of AI conversations are excluded from industry-standard productivity reports, which prioritize work-related use cases.

Independent analysis shows that non-work interactions frequently involve sensitive topics, including health, relationships, harassment, and sexual content, which are often omitted from corporate disclosures.
Current AI policy and risk assessments are being built on limited, curated datasets, creating a blind spot for researchers and regulators regarding the true societal impact of generative models.
The study suggests that relying solely on vendor-provided data, such as the Anthropic Economic Index, provides an incomplete picture of how consumers actually integrate AI into their daily lives.

backlog.title: Nvidia Backs OpenAI Data Center, Anthropic News, Google Buys Spirit Airlines Data

The convergence of hardware investment, rapid revenue scaling in AI labs, and the commoditization of corporate data underscores the evolving 'data is oil' thesis in the current tech landscape.

backlog.title: The role of the astronaut is in flux
backlog.summary: When the four astronauts on board NASA’s Artemis II swung around the moon earlier this year, they set a new record for the farthest humans have ever ventured from Earth, surpassing the distance set by Apollo 13 in 1972 by some 4,000 miles.  While no space mission can live up to the historic touchdown of…
bullets: Human spaceflight is entering a new era with the Artemis program and private sector initiatives, yet the fundamental economic and scientific justification for human presence versus robotics remains debated.
Geopolitical competition between the US-led Artemis program and the China-Russia lunar base partnership is driving a new space race focused on establishing permanent lunar infrastructure.

The commercialization of space, led by companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin, is shifting the role of the astronaut from purely scientific exploration toward potential tourism and extraterrestrial resource mining.
